claim: DR47-1's placement ruling (arm the reorder tracker inside beginTravelRecording, past its same-pointer early return) makes the shield's recorded surviving-recording residual capable of committing a structural write against an oid the user never dragged, and acceptance 46 codifies that state as GREEN without asserting anything about what the next release does. CONVERGENT: the critic lane reached this independently.
evidence: The early return `if (incomingId === null || incomingId === active.pointerId) return;` fires BEFORE the closure DR47-1 designates as the arming site. On the WC-1/WC-2 path the shield's own docblock records as live, a second press of the same pointerId — the ordinary case for a mouse, where pointerId never varies — arms NO tracker; gesture 1's tracker stays live holding gesture 1's press point and press target. Gesture 1's tracker shares the surviving document-capture pointermove, so gesture 2's moves feed it, and gesture 2's pointerup reaches onGestureEnd then stop(), which is the plan's release/commit point. Under DR47-12 the subject is the press target — gesture 1's. Acceptance 46 states the outcome plainly: exactly ONE live recording and ONE live reorder tracker, and they are the same gesture's — i.e. the first gesture's. Section 3.2 disposes of this with an assertion, not a trace, and the residual appears nowhere in the pre-mortem or the residual-risk section.
impact: At HEAD this residual costs a mis-swallowed click. Under phase-47 it costs a move-up/move-down POST on an element the user did not touch, a blue line painted over a different parent, and a swallowed selecting click — the silent-wrong-write class DR47-12 and Principle 3 exist to forbid, re-entered through the ruling chosen to avoid it. Acceptance 46 is the only gate over this path and it asserts counts, not the write, so the defect ships green.
required_correction: Rule the reorder tracker's lifetime independently of the recording's same-pointer early return — either re-seed the tracker (press target, press point, state) on EVERY ordinary press even when the recording itself is a no-op, or have the early-return path tear the stale tracker down. State the placement against the specific statement in the closure that the mutation moves, and replace acceptance 46's count-only assertion with an OUTCOME leg plus a Path: after a lost-terminal gesture on element A, a second same-pointer press-and-drag on element B must POST B's oid or nothing, never A's, and must not swallow B's selecting click.

claim: Acceptance 32 — the only gate over the owner-mandated B-Q4 deliverable — cannot go RED, because its Path asserts a fixture property this phase's design does not produce.
evidence: The stated RED-when is 'freeze it at the press box, so it stops tracking a reflowing element', with the Path 'the fixture is a parent whose siblings reflow as the drag proceeds'. Nothing in the phase reflows anything during a drag: DR47-13's state table gives engaged exactly the blue line plus the W x H readout and no DOM move; DR47-8 puts both nodes in a new #dsh-reorder-layer that is pointer-events: none and a sibling of the page tree; DR47-10 rules S47-3 ships FULL paint and NO write, and the write only lands at S47-4 after release. With the page DOM untouched for the whole gesture, the dragged element's box at any mid-drag sample is byte-identical to its press-time box, so the frozen and live readings agree and the mutation is unobservable. The plan names no mechanism by which such a fixture is built.
impact: One of the three items the owner put in scope ships with a gate that reads green whether or not the readout tracks anything, and the plan's marked claim that the fixture reflows would be carried into a lane's brief as a re-read fact. This is a further instance of the class the plan opens by ruling against, in the round that rules it.
required_correction: Either state the mechanism that makes the dragged element's box change during a paint-only drag and cite it, or restate the mutation so it reaches a real assertion — drive a viewport resize or a scroll mid-gesture and assert the readout's sampled text tracks it, or key the leg on a quantity that genuinely varies during the drag. If neither is available, mark the Path NONE — non-discriminating and say what would have to be built, per the plan's own two-answer rule.

claim: A reorder tracker armed inside the shared travel recording survives a lost terminal and can commit a structural write against an element the user is no longer touching; the plan affirmatively ACCEPTS this state in acceptance 46 instead of refusing it, and no gate can see it. CONVERGENT: the architect lane reached this independently.
evidence: The recording's own docblock records the residual — a surviving recording keeps measuring from the CANCELLED gesture's press point, so the next gesture's origin is a point the user's finger never touched — narrowed by WC-1/WC-2 but explicitly not removed. The mechanics: the same-pointer early return makes the NEXT press a no-op so no fresh tracker is armed; the surviving gesture's onTravel listener checks neither button state nor pointer-down state; and onGestureEnd/ownsGesture means the next pointerup of that same pointer terminates and therefore RELEASES gesture 1. Under DR47-2 the reorder tracker shares that one stream, one stop() and one set of terminals, and DR47-13 makes commit happen at release. So after any lost terminal, an ordinary mouse traverse with no button down crosses the engage threshold from a stale origin, engages, paints the line, and the user's next click commits against press-1's oid. A grep for button, pointercancel, surviving and WC-1 over the plan returns nothing that gates this.
impact: Under HEAD this residual costs a swallowed click. Phase-47 escalates the identical residual to a silent write to page.tsx moving an element the user never dragged — the outcome DR47-12 exists to prevent, reached through the door DR47-1/DR47-2 open, and against Principle 1. It is also unreviewable as specified, because the plan's gate for this path measures tracker count rather than write reachability.
required_correction: Rule an explicit tracker-liveness condition that does not inherit the recording's same-pointer early return — the tracker dropped unconditionally at every press in the same first-statements block the swallow cell is drained in and re-armed only by a press that reaches the ordinary arm, and/or engagement and commit requiring the primary button still down, read from the move/up event. Add an acceptance criterion that drives press-with-no-terminal, then a pointer traverse, then an ordinary press-and-click, asserting POST count 0, zero insertion-line nodes and HEAD-identical selection, with the RED-when being removal of that condition and a stated Path to the POST-count assertion. Acceptance 46 must assert write-unreachability, not tracker count.

claim: The plan uses 'armed' in two incompatible senses, and under DR47-13's own definition acceptance 8 — the gate protecting the shipped Shift/multi-select swallow, and DR47-2's declared stop boundary — cannot go RED as traced.
evidence: DR47-13's state table defines armed as an ordinary press with NO modifiers, inside the widened recording. Acceptance 10 asserts Cmd/Ctrl/Alt drags arm zero reorder gestures. But acceptance 8's Path asserts the opposite for its mutation to reach its assertion: the reorder tracker runs on every move of every ordinary gesture including Shift gestures, and nothing gates the tracker out of a Shift drag. Both cannot be true. If armed means what the state table says, a Shift press arms no tracker, the mutation never executes during a Shift drag, and the swallow verdict does not move — the gate is non-discriminating. If instead the tracker attaches on every ordinary press and only the STATE is modifier-gated, then acceptance 10's 'zero armed' and the arming-count assertions 2-5 and 46 are all counting something the plan has not defined.
impact: Acceptance 8 is the only gate pinning that the widened two-consumer stream leaves the shipped travel number byte-identical for non-reorder gestures — the phase's highest-risk regression surface, on the file whose docblock records that arm-table errors are detectable only by measurement. A stop boundary whose gate cannot fire is scaffolding.
required_correction: Define one vocabulary — state explicitly whether a Shift/Cmd/Alt press attaches a reorder tracker to the stream at all, distinguish 'attached to the stream' from the armed STATE with two different words, and re-derive acceptances 2-5, 8, 9, 10 and 46 against the chosen definition. Acceptance 8's Path must then name a mutation that provably executes during the gesture whose swallow verdict it asserts.

claim: S47-4 states a fact about this tree that is false and contradicts S47-1.
evidence: S47-4's Touches line says packages/descvi/src/react/overlay/__tests__/ is a stale path holding no-next.test.ts alone. That directory holds 99 entries, and no-next.test.ts lives in packages/descvi/src/__tests__/, a different directory. S47-1's own Touches line places its new unit test file under packages/descvi/src/react/overlay/__tests__/. The lead independently confirmed both counts in this tree.
impact: A plan whose governing discipline is 'cite what you re-read' carries an unverified repo claim that declares S47-1's own chosen test home stale, inviting a lane to relocate S47-1's gates away from the 99 sibling overlay tests. The consequential half of the ruling — sidecar gates belong in packages/descvi/test/sidecar/ — is correct and should survive the correction.
required_correction: Replace the warning's justification with the true one (the sidecar harness lives in packages/descvi/test/sidecar/; a sidecar gate under the overlay __tests__/ tree would mint a second sidecar home) and delete the false claim about that directory's contents.
